name: food
description: Look up a packaged food by its barcode, search for products, compare them side by side and check a product's listed allergens.

interface.longDescription:
Look up a packaged food by its barcode, search for products, compare them side by side and check a product's listed allergens.

Ask "what is in the product with barcode 3017620422003?", "find oat milks sold in France", "which of these three barcodes has the least sugar?" or "does this product contain milk or nuts?".

Food Facts reads Open Food Facts, a free database that people around the world add to by scanning and photographing labels.

A product answer shows the name, brand, size, ingredients, the allergens and traces the entry lists, the Nutri-Score and NOVA group when known, and nutrition per 100 g (energy, fat, saturated fat, carbohydrates, sugars, fibre, protein, salt and sodium).

Because the data is crowd-sourced, it can be incomplete, wrong or out of date, and recipes change. Every answer says how complete the entry looks and reminds you that the physical label wins, especially for allergies.

The allergen check reads the entry's listed allergen tags and its ingredients text. It is a data lookup, not a safety guarantee, and not dietary or medical advice.

Coverage is strongest in France and Europe and thinner in the US and Asia. For recalls of food products, use the Recalls plugin.

Data © Open Food Facts contributors, available under the Open Database Licence (ODbL) v1.0. It stores nothing about you: answers are cached for a few hours, and the only lasting record is a daily count of calls per tool.
capabilities: Looks up a product by EAN or UPC barcode after checking the barcode's check digit
Shows ingredients, listed allergens and traces, Nutri-Score and NOVA group
Shows nutrition per 100 g: energy, fat, saturated fat, carbohydrates, sugars, fibre, protein, salt, sodium
Searches products by name or brand, optionally limited to a country
Compares up to five products by sugars, salt or energy per 100 g
Checks a product's listed allergens against the ones you want to avoid
Says how complete the entry is and reminds you to check the physical label
defaultPrompt: What is in the product with barcode 3017620422003?
Find oat milks sold in France
Does barcode 5449000000996 contain milk or nuts?

positive.description: status ok with the name Nutella, brands, ingredients text, allergens (milk, nuts, soybeans), Nutri-Score, NOVA group 4, nutrition per 100 g, a data_quality_note and the Open Food Facts link, with the Open Food Facts attribution and the reminder to check the physical label. Check against: https://world.openfoodfacts.org/api/v2/product/3017620422003.json
positive.prompt: What is in the product with barcode 3017620422003?

positive.description: status ok and a list of products, each with barcode, name, brands and Nutri-Score, taken from entries sold in France. Check against: https://search.openfoodfacts.org/search?q=oat milk countries_tags:"en:france"
positive.prompt: Find oat milks sold in France.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_products with query "oat milk" and country "France".

positive.description: status ok and a ranking from lowest to highest sugars per 100 g with each product's name, value and Nutri-Score, stating the basis is per 100 g. Check against: https://world.openfoodfacts.org/api/v2/search?code=3017620422003,5449000000996
positive.prompt: Which has less sugar per 100 g: 3017620422003 or 5449000000996?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls compare_products with barcodes ["3017620422003", "5449000000996"] and field "sugars".

positive.description: status ok with milk under contains and peanuts under not_listed, the allergens the entry lists, and the reminder that this is crowd-sourced data and the physical label wins. Check against: https://world.openfoodfacts.org/api/v2/product/3017620422003.json
positive.prompt: Does barcode 3017620422003 contain milk or peanuts?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls check_allergens with barcode "3017620422003" and avoid ["milk", "peanuts"].

positive.description: status invalid_barcode with a message that the check digit is wrong, without contacting Open Food Facts. Check against: none: the check digit is validated locally
positive.prompt: Is 1234567890123 a real barcode? What product is it?

negative.description: The plugin reads community-contributed data and gives no safety or medical advice. Expected: Does not declare the product safe. If a barcode is given it may run check_allergens, but it says the data is crowd-sourced and not a guarantee, and tells the user to read the physical label and ask their doctor.
negative.prompt: Is it safe for my child with a severe peanut allergy to eat this chocolate bar?

negative.description: The plugin looks up packaged product data; it does not plan diets or give nutrition or medical guidance. Expected: Does not call a tool. Says it cannot give diet or medical advice and suggests a dietitian or doctor.
negative.prompt: Plan me a 1,800 calorie vegetarian diet for the week to lose weight.

negative.description: Recalls are not in Open Food Facts; the Recalls plugin covers them. Expected: Does not use the Open Food Facts tools to answer about recalls. Says this plugin has no recall data.
negative.prompt: Has this brand of peanut butter been recalled?

publication.release_notes: First release. Reads Open Food Facts: barcode lookup, product search, comparison per 100 g and allergen check. Answers are cached for a few hours; read-only, no sign-in.
